今天的主题：金钱、消费和债务。这组词对 G 类很实用：大作文常考「年轻人该不该用信用卡」「政府是否该教学生理财」；小作文常写给银行或房东的信，比如解释晚交房租、申请分期还款；口语 Part 1 的 Money、Shopping，Part 2「描述一次你存钱买东西的经历」都能直接用。

例句

  • Many young people get into debt because they rely too much on credit cards.（很多年轻人因为太依赖信用卡而欠债。）
  • We need to cut our monthly expenses and stick to a strict budget.（我们得削减每月开支，严格按预算来。）
  • He took out a loan to pay the deposit on his first flat.（他贷了款来付第一套公寓的首付。）
  • I am writing to ask whether I could pay the rent in monthly instalments.（我写信想问一下能不能按月分期付房租。）
  • Schools should teach teenagers how to manage money so that they don't face financial problems later.（学校应该教青少年理财，免得他们以后遇到经济问题。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 debt、budget、afford 写一句你对年轻人用信用卡的看法，大作文能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Living with debt（背着债务生活）。这集讲英国人负债有多普遍，一个叫 Jason 的年轻人工资不够养家只能一次次贷款，还有社会学家 Ryan Davey 住进低收入社区几个月，听居民讲他们怎样勉强维持收支。这集语速比较平稳，而且主持人会把每个短语解释一遍，比较好跟。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：英国成年人通过信用卡、透支和个人贷款平均欠多少钱？a) £2,200 b) £4,200 c) £6,200。顺便听出：2025 年每天有多少人联系公民咨询局求助债务？杰森说除了什么以外看不到出路？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Jason 和 Ryan Davey 两段是真实录音，语速稍快，多听几遍。
  4. 第三遍挑 Jason 那段（"Whatever jobs there are aren't enough..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：pay back / pay off / clear a debt（还债）、make ends meet（勉强维持收支）、in arrears（拖欠）、on the never-never（分期付款买）、financial strain（经济压力）、take out a loan（贷款）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Neil：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

Neil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是尼尔。

Pippa：And I'm Pippa. Are you good at saving money, Neil? Or do you like to spend it?

Pippa：我是皮帕。尼尔，你擅长存钱吗？还是更喜欢花钱？

Neil：Well, actually, a bit of both. I like to spend money on nice things, but I also try to save, mainly because I've got children. How about you?

Neil：其实两样都有点。我喜欢把钱花在好东西上，但我也会尽量存钱，主要是因为我有孩子。你呢？

Pippa：Yeah, I'm the same. I like to save money, or I try to, for the future. But I also do spend it. I don't count every penny每分钱都算计 that I spend and save every single penny便士 that I earn.

Pippa：我也一样。我喜欢为将来存钱，或者说我努力这么做。但我也确实会花。我不会花一分钱都算计，也不会赚的每一分钱都存起来。

Neil：Mmm. Well, whether you're a saver or a spender, being in debt债务 is common in the UK. Debt债务 refers to指的是 money a person has borrowed借入 to buy something and which they have to pay back还钱, usually to a bank, a credit card company信用卡公司, or another person.

Neil：嗯。不管你是爱存钱的还是爱花钱的，在英国负债都很常见。债务指的是一个人为了买东西借来的、必须还回去的钱，通常是欠银行、信用卡公司或者别人的。

Pippa：Many people avoid talking about debt债务, but it affects us all. In 2025, over 1000 people contacted the UK Citizens Advice Bureau公民咨询局（英国免费咨询机构） every single day of the year for help with their debt债务. And when debt债务 gets out of control失控, it causes stress and worry. BBC Radio 4 programme Thinking Allowed interviewed one young man, Jason, about his debt债务.

Pippa：很多人不愿谈债务，但它影响着我们每个人。2025 年，全年每天都有超过 1000 人联系英国公民咨询局，寻求债务方面的帮助。债务一旦失控，就会带来压力和焦虑。BBC 广播四台的节目《Thinking Allowed》采访了一个叫杰森的年轻人，聊他的债务。

Jason：Whatever jobs there are aren't enough to provide for a family养家. Sometimes you need to take out loans贷款. I've done it a few times, but you can't ever pay it back. You can't see a way out出路, other than winning the lottery彩票 or something. I'd like to think I could clear them all one day, even if it means, like, five years paying them off把它们还清.

Jason：现有的那些工作都不够养家。有时候你不得不去贷款。我贷过好几次，可是怎么也还不清。除了中彩票之类的，根本看不到出路。我希望有一天能把它们全部还清，哪怕要花个五年慢慢还。

Neil：Jason uses three phrases, pay back还钱, pay off还清, and clear debt债务, all of which mean the same thing – to give back the money you've borrowed借入.

Neil：杰森用了三个短语：pay back、pay off 和 clear debt，意思都一样，就是把借的钱还回去。

Pippa：In this episode, we'll hear more about living with debt债务 by learning some useful new words and phrases. And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary used, plus a quiz and worksheet练习题, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Pippa：这一集我们会通过学一些有用的新词和短语，多聊聊背着债务生活是什么样。别忘了，所有词汇以及小测验和练习题都在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上。

Neil：But first, I have a question for you, Pippa. According to debt债务 support group The Money Charity, roughly how much is the average British adult in debt债务 through credit cards信用卡, overdrafts透支 and personal loans贷款? Is it: a) £2,200, b) £4,200, or c) £6,200?

Neil：不过首先，我要问你个问题，皮帕。根据债务援助组织 The Money Charity 的数据，英国成年人通过信用卡、透支和个人贷款平均大约欠多少钱？是 a) 2200 英镑，b) 4200 英镑，还是 c) 6200 英镑？

Pippa：Hmm. I'm not sure. I'll say £2,200.

Pippa：嗯，我不太确定。我选 2200 英镑。

Neil：OK. Well, we will find out弄清楚，得知 the answer later in the programme. Jason's story features in a new book by sociologist社会学家 Ryan Davey. Ryan spent months living in a low-income housing estate低收入住宅区, which he gave the fictional虚构的 name Woldham. He talked with residents居民 and listened to their money worries. Here, Ryan explains more to BBC Radio 4's Thinking Allowed:

Neil：好，答案节目后面揭晓。杰森的故事出现在社会学家瑞安·戴维的一本新书里。瑞安在一个低收入住宅区住了好几个月，他给那里起了个虚构的名字叫 Woldham。他和居民聊天，听他们的金钱烦恼。下面瑞安在 BBC 广播四台的《Thinking Allowed》里详细讲讲：

Ryan Davey：My approach was to let people know that I was interested in learning about their lives and how they were making ends meet勉强维持收支, so I did some interviews with residents居民, and I paid attention to where debt债务 came up被提到 in everyday conversations. For many people in Woldham, Jason included, debt债务 was an ordinary feature of daily life. And beyond that, being in arrears拖欠 – so, being behind with one or more monthly payment commitments承诺；（定期要付的）款项 – was part of daily life.

Ryan Davey：我的做法是让大家知道，我想了解他们的生活，了解他们是怎么勉强维持收支的。所以我采访了一些居民，并留意日常聊天里什么时候会提到债务。对 Woldham 的很多人来说，包括杰森，债务是日常生活中很平常的一部分。不仅如此，拖欠款项，也就是一笔或几笔每月该付的钱没按时付，也是日常生活的一部分。

Pippa：The people of Woldham were making ends meet勉强维持收支. To make ends meet勉强维持收支 means having just enough money to pay for basic living expenses开支 like food, bills and rent.

Pippa：Woldham 的人们都在勉强维持生计。make ends meet 的意思是钱刚好够付基本生活开支，比如吃饭、账单和房租。

Neil：Ryan found that many residents居民 were in arrears拖欠, a phrase meaning to still owe欠（钱） money that should have already been repaid偿还. For most residents居民, debt债务 was a normal part of daily life.

Neil：瑞安发现很多居民都处于拖欠状态，in arrears 这个短语的意思是本该已经还上的钱还欠着。对大多数居民来说，债务是日常生活的正常部分。

Pippa：With a regular income, debt债务 can be managed, but for those who are unemployed失业的 or on low incomes收入低, it can cause serious distress痛苦，苦恼. Here, Ryan discusses how the residents居民 he met felt about their debt债务 with BBC Radio 4's Thinking Allowed:

Pippa：有稳定收入的话，债务还能应付；但对失业或者收入低的人来说，债务会带来很大的痛苦。下面瑞安在《Thinking Allowed》里聊聊他遇到的居民对自己的债务有什么感受：

Ryan Davey：Jason actually fluctuated波动，摇摆 between wanting to clear all of his debts债务 on the one hand一方面, and on the other what he described as living on the never-never分期付款（口语） and actually questioning the supposed所谓的 moral obligation道德义务 to pay his debts债务. Over the months that I knew him, the financial strain经济压力 on him and his partner increased. They missed some of their bills. Their internet was disconnected切断（服务）.

Ryan Davey：杰森其实一直在摇摆：一方面想把所有债还清，另一方面又过着他所说的「分期度日」的生活，甚至质疑所谓还债的道德义务。在我认识他的那几个月里，他和伴侣的经济压力越来越大。他们有些账单没交上，家里的网也被断了。

Neil：Jason was living on the never-never分期付款（口语）, an informal非正式的，口语的 phrase for buying the things you need by making regular small payments over a long time. It's called the never-never分期付款（口语） because it seems the debt债务 will never be repaid偿还.

Neil：杰森过着 the never-never 的生活，这是个口语说法，指靠长期定期小额分期付款来买需要的东西。之所以叫 never-never，是因为这笔债好像永远也还不完。

Pippa：Jason experienced financial strain经济压力 – emotional stress caused by a lack of money to meet his basic needs or to repay偿还 his debt债务. Debt债务 is a serious issue. It affects many people and there are support groups援助组织 who can help if you need it. OK. Neil, what was the answer to your question?

Pippa：杰森承受着经济压力，也就是因为钱不够满足基本需要或还债而产生的精神压力。债务是个严肃的问题，影响很多人，如果你需要，有援助组织可以帮忙。好，尼尔，你那道题的答案是什么？

Neil：I asked what the average amount of debt债务 a British adult has through credit cards信用卡, overdrafts透支 and personal loans贷款.

Neil：我问的是英国成年人通过信用卡、透支和个人贷款平均欠多少钱。

Pippa：I said it was around £2,200.

Pippa：我说大约 2200 英镑。

Neil：I'm afraid that's not the right answer. In fact, it's £4,232. OK. Let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with debt债务 – money a person has borrowed借入 and needs to give back.

Neil：恐怕答错了。实际上是 4232 英镑。好，我们来回顾一下学过的词，先是 debt，指一个人借来、需要还的钱。

Pippa：The phrases to pay back还钱, to pay off还清, and to clear a debt债务 all mean to give back money you have borrowed借入.

Pippa：pay back、pay off 和 clear a debt 这几个短语都表示把借的钱还回去。

Neil：If someone is making ends meet勉强维持收支, they have just enough money to pay for basic living expenses开支. And if they are in arrears拖欠, they still owe欠（钱） money that should have been repaid偿还 already.

Neil：如果一个人在 making ends meet，说明他的钱刚好够付基本生活开支。如果一个人 in arrears，说明他还欠着本该早就还上的钱。

Pippa：If you buy something on the never-never分期付款（口语）, you buy it by making small regular payments over a long period.

Pippa：如果你 on the never-never 买东西，就是在很长一段时间里定期小额分期付款来买。

Neil：And finally, financial strain经济压力 is emotional stress caused by a lack of money to meet your basic needs.

Neil：最后，financial strain 指因为钱不够满足基本需要而产生的精神压力。

Pippa：Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to know how debt债务 is spelled and all the other words from this episode, visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to find a full vocabulary list.

Pippa：我们的六分钟又到了。如果你想知道 debt 怎么拼，以及这集里的其他所有单词，请访问我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com，那里有完整的词汇表。

Neil：See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.

Neil：下次见，今天就到这里，再见。

Pippa：Bye!

Pippa：拜拜！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（英国负债普遍、Jason 的经历、Woldham 社区的居民怎样过日子），6 个表达都知道意思，Jason 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. After losing his job, he found it hard to make ends ______.（维持收支）
  2. It took me five years to pay ______ my student loan.（还清）
  3. The tenant is two months in ______ with the rent.（拖欠）
  4. Rising prices have put a lot of financial ______ on young families.（压力）
  5. We had to take ______ a loan to buy a new car.（贷款）
  6. I can't ______ to go on holiday this year; I need to save money.（负担得起）
点开看答案

开头那题选 b，实际是 £4,232。皮帕猜的是 £2,200，猜错了。2025 年每天有超过 1000 人联系公民咨询局；杰森说除了中彩票之类的看不到出路。填空：1. meet 2. off（back 也行）3. arrears 4. strain 5. out 6. afford

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：Should young people be allowed to use credit cards? 用英语说两三句：In my opinion, ... / The main reason is that ...。也可以想想：你自己更像 saver 还是 spender？
